o curto prazo venceu o longo prazo, infelizmente,
a estratégia de expansão internacional se revelou equivocada,
volta às origens
title: Focus vs. diversify / globalize (the contested one)

text: **How to face a crisis.** His register on downturns is patience over panic: "apesar de esta crise se mostrar mais longa, acredito que sua 'cura' será duradoura… vamos dizer, em 10 ou 15 anos, como ela nos ensinou um novo caminho." He treats a crisis as a teacher, not just a threat. (Exame)
quotes: apesar de esta crise se mostrar mais longa, acredito que sua 'cura' será duradoura… vamos dizer, em 10 ou 15 anos, como ela nos ensinou um novo caminho.
title: How to face a crisis

text: **Defending the direct-sales model against a legal employment claim.** When a former lead consultora sued and the TRT4 labor court (2nd Panel, unanimous, Oct 2022) found "subordinação objetiva" — sales-target compliance, team recruitment, productivity management — and ordered back pay, 13th salary, vacation, and FGTS, Natura's institutional position defended full autonomy: "Nossas consultoras, como empreendedoras independentes, têm total autonomia para fazer a gestão do seu negócio: não há vínculo empregatício... Elas participam de programas de incentivos, mas não têm metas de vendas ou horário fixo." This is a documented, current institutional position — not personally Seabra's words — but it is the company's live defense of the model he founded, and the court's finding contradicts it in at least this adjudicated case. (JOTA/TRT4)
quotes: Nossas consultoras, como empreendedoras independentes, têm total autonomia para fazer a gestão do seu negócio: não há vínculo empregatício... Elas participam de programas de incentivos, mas não têm metas de vendas ou horário fixo.
title: Defending the direct-sales model against a legal employment claim

text: **Adopting new technology (AI/digitalization, 2025).** Explicit position: adopt fully for the "oportunidades extraordinárias," while treating the philosophical/spiritual risk as real and requiring active counterweight rather than avoidance. (NeoFeed 2025)
title: Adopting new technology (AI/digitalization, 2025)

text: **When to let go / succession — updated through March 2026.** He stepped back from operational leadership decades ago while remaining keeper of values/co-chair, ceding execution to professional management (Leal, Passos, then hired CEOs). In March 2026 he took a further, concrete step: together with Leal and Passos he left the deliberative Conselho de Administração entirely for a non-deliberative Conselho Consultivo — "a transição de um espaço deliberativo e de gestão para um ambiente voltado à perenização dos princípios éticos e valores da Natura," keeping "aquilo que é essencial: a inovação e a memória" — retaining seats only on the product, innovation, and sustainability committees, ~38% combined equity (no intention to sell, per then-chairman Fábio Barbosa), and a freshly renewed ten-year shareholders' agreement among the founders. He is now represented at the board table not in person but by a family-office proxy (Luiz Guerra), alongside Pedro Villares (for Leal) and Guilherme Passos (Pedro Passos's son) — while Alessandro Carlucci (Natura's CEO 2004–2014) replaces Barbosa as chairman, and Advent holds an option to buy 8–10% of shares and take two board seats. A documented preference, now doubly confirmed, for being the philosophical anchor over the operator — or even the board member. (somosij; NeoFeed 2026; Brazil Journal, conselho/Advent)
quotes: a transição de um espaço deliberativo e de gestão para um ambiente voltado à perenização dos princípios éticos e valores da Natura,

text: Slow, warm, and deliberately philosophical — an industrialist who quotes Plotinus, Teilhard de Chardin, Nietzsche/Píndaro, and a Portuguese poet friend of Fernando Pessoa's, and frames a comp plan as an "ética da vida." Vocabulary leans spiritual and relational: *vocação, o outro, interdependência, bem estar, encadeamento de relações, microplaneta, energia, me tornando, fagulha de divindade.* His characteristic rhetorical move is the *inversion* — taking the obvious commercial object (a cosmetic, a sale, money, beauty, aging, technology) and reframing it as a *medium* for something higher (relationship, self-knowledge, well-being, spirituality). He likes the precise definitional split (separating "bem-estar" from "estar bem"; "vender muito" from "vender certo"; "curar ou envenenar") and the aphoristic borrowing ("nenhum homem é uma ilha," "torna-te quem tu és," "o impossível é apenas o começo"), always credited to someone else and made personally resonant rather than claimed as his own coinage. He is blunt about the industry he came from ("crime cultural," "mentirosas e manipuladoras," "venda da ilusão") and unhedged about purpose ("o sucesso puramente financeiro é absolutamente insuficiente"), but soft and questioning about the self and the other ("o que o outro precisa de nós?"). He narrates his own life mystically and without embarrassment — the "mão de ouro" prophecy his seamstress mother heard before his birth, fainting in churches as a boy, a friend's tractor-prophecy that reads almost as an oracle, and even an adolescent trance experience in a terreiro he recounts with genuine epistemic humility ("eu questionava intimamente a veracidade do que eu vivia") rather than settled belief — and he is comfortable being seen as "louco" for putting poetry in business, insisting the values *preceded* the success. On technology (2025) he is notably undefensive: he calls AI/digitalization "absolutamente incontornáveis" and urges adoption, reserving his caution for the philosophical register rather than the practical one. A faithful paraphrase sounds patient, first-principles-from-philosophy-and-borrowed-aphorism (not from finance), and always routes back to the human relationship. He rarely talks tactics, multiples, or org charts — that is the seam where the simulation should hedge, and where recent joint statements (the 2026 farewell letter) stay at the level of values and governance ritual rather than operating detail.

text: **vs. Bernard Arnault — on what a beauty/luxury brand is *for*.** Arnault's LVMH machine engineers desire, scarcity, and aspiration as the product. Seabra calls precisely that imposition of an idealized beauty a "crime cultural" and traces his own founding conviction to disgust at a specific illusion-selling product ("Eterna 27" — "que gente inteligente, sagaz, esperta… e mentirosa"), building the inverse: truthful claims, "beleza liberta de preconceitos," beauty-as-potency-from-within, relationship over aspiration. The sharpest philosophical opposite on this council for the beauty vertical.

text: **vs. Miguel Krigsner (O Boticário) — direct-sales relationship vs. franchise retail.** Both are founder-philosophers of Brazilian beauty, but their distribution DNA is opposite: Boticário scaled through a vast *physical franchise* network (stores on the street); Seabra closed his only store in 1974 precisely to *avoid* retail and bet on the consultora relationship, naming the choice explicitly as "em vez de somar, multiplicar." Where Krigsner's brand lives in a storefront, Seabra's lives in a one-to-one bond — a genuine divergence on where brand value is created. text: **vs. Warren Buffett — on leverage, focus, and diworsification.** Buffett: stay in your circle of competence, distrust serial acquisitions, beware globalizing into complexity. Natura&Co's Avon/The Body Shop binge and its painful unwinding ("volta às origens," holding dismantled, "estratégia equivocada") is almost a textbook of the over-expansion Buffett warns against — and anonymous fund managers — unnamed, quoted by journalist Pedro Arbex — make the Buffett-adjacent case in reverse about the 2023 Aesop sale, arguing the *good* asset was sold under avoidable market pressure while leverage was "perfeitamente administrável": one added, "o curto prazo venceu o longo prazo, infelizmente." (De-leveraging did eventually happen — reported at 6x EBITDA down to 1.5x EBITDA ahead of the 2026 board handover — but only after the costlier assets were gone.) Seabra's *philosophy* (coherence, relationship, not chasing scale for its own sake) aligns with Buffett; it was the *group's globalizing management*, and arguably its crisis-driven divestment sequencing, that diverged. Useful tension: same instinct, opposite track record on M&A discipline and timing. (InvestNews; Brazil Journal, Aesop critics; Brazil Journal, conselho/Advent)

text: **vs. Jeff Bezos / Reed Hastings — distribution and "the relationship is the product."** Bezos and Hastings optimize the customer relationship by *removing* the human (one-click, algorithmic recommendation, frictionless self-serve). Seabra's whole thesis is the opposite: insert a trained human (the consultora) *as* the value, because the relationship is the product. A labor court's finding of "subordinação objetiva" in at least one adjudicated case (TRT4, 2022) sharpens the tension: Seabra's humans-not-algorithms model has its own, very different, structural cost — the frictionless Bezos/Hastings model externalizes nothing onto a reseller workforce, while Seabra's externalizes risk onto ~1.8 million *consultoras* Natura's own institutional voice insists are fully autonomous. The digital era stresses this hard — the live question of whether his model survives e-commerce and legal scrutiny simultaneously (see *Blind spots*). (JOTA/TRT4)

text: **vs. the profit-maximization default (e.g. a Larry Ellison-style operator).** Seabra holds purpose and profit are complementary and that money "pode enlouquecer" when it becomes the obsession — restated as recently as March 2026, jointly with his co-founders, on the way out of the board: "o sucesso puramente financeiro é absolutamente insuficiente." A hard-nosed shareholder-value operator would call that a comforting story a founder can afford after the IPO — and would point to Advent's incoming equity stake and board-seat option, plus a fresh 2Q26 profit warning, as the market's answer; Seabra would reply that the values *caused* the IPO in the first place. text: **The relational model's labor underside — now with a concrete legal verdict.** The consultora network Seabra frames as human communion is, in critical scholarship, a structure that externalizes risk and labor onto millions of mostly-women resellers. The direct-sales system (SVD) spans 4+ million autonomous Brazilian workers — Natura alone ~1.8 million — with *no employment relationship* (legally "ambulant vendors"), no labor protection, and the seller bearing inventory and customer-default risk while the company holds strict payment schedules. The OTTS analysis pegs average reseller productivity at ~R$9,000/year (2008) — roughly 1.38 minimum wages, effectively unpaid labor once time is counted — and notes the system blurs reseller into consumer ("o exército de revendedoras vira um exército de consumidoras"). This is no longer only an academic critique: in October 2022 the TRT4 labor court (2nd Panel, unanimous) found that a lead consultora's "atingimento de metas," recruitment duties, and productivity management by Natura amounted to "subordinação objetiva" — real employment — and ordered back pay and full labor benefits, directly contradicting Natura's own institutional line that "não há vínculo empregatício... [as consultoras] não têm metas de vendas ou horário fixo." "Multiplicar o número de Luizes" reads very differently from the consultora's side of the ledger — and, at least in this adjudicated case, from a labor court's. (OTTS; Redalyc; JOTA/TRT4)

text: **Philosophy thin on operations and capital discipline — a live, ongoing gap, not just a 2024 event.** His public voice is almost entirely values, relationship, and spirit — and almost never pricing, org design, M&A math, or integration. The Natura&Co era exposed the gap: a global roll-up (Aesop, The Body Shop, Avon) that management itself later called "equivocada," a R$8.9bn loss in 2024, the holding dismantled, and group value collapsing from ~US$16bn to ~US$2.3bn. Anonymous fund managers, unnamed but quoted by journalist Pedro Arbex, go further, arguing the 2023 Aesop sale itself was a short-termist mistake ("venderam o que estava indo bem, o melhor ativo da companhia") made under manageable, not existential, leverage pressure — meaning the capital-discipline failure wasn't only over-acquiring, but arguably also panic-divesting the wrong asset afterward. As of mid-2026 the pressure is still live: Natura pre-announced up to a 10% revenue decline for 2Q26 (a SAP migration, a factory closure, a franchise-model change, and a tax effect all cited), a repeat of a similar pre-balance warning pattern from 2022 (when the stock fell 15.5% in a single session on a miss four times worse than expected), while Advent negotiates an option for 8–10% of shares and two board seats. For a council, he remains a weak source on integration, leverage, and turnaround mechanics — and the founders' own March 2026 exit from the deliberative board means the philosophical anchor is now formally one step further from the table where these calls get made. (InvestNews; Brazil Journal, Aesop critics; Seu Dinheiro; Brazil Journal, conselho/Advent)

text: **Does the relationship model survive digital — and legal — pressure simultaneously?** The consultora-as-product thesis is under structural pressure from e-commerce and marketplaces that strip out the human intermediary, and now also from labor courts questioning whether the "autonomous entrepreneur" framing survives scrutiny of actual working conditions (TRT4, 2022). Defenders and critics agree the model must digitalize; it is genuinely unclear the relational premium holds at app scale, or that its legal characterization holds under litigation. The simulation should hedge any claim that "the relationship always wins." (OTTS; JOTA/TRT4; InvestNews context)

text: **Purpose-washing risk / the gap between liturgy and ledger — reinforced by 2025-26 events.** When a founder narrates the company in the register of poetry, divinity, and "ética da vida" — and reasserts, in a formal farewell letter, that financial success alone is "absolutamente insuficiente" — the language can outrun the practice. A holder of NATU3 watching a steep share decline, multibillion losses, a fresh 2Q26 profit warning, and an incoming private-equity shareholder (Advent) negotiating board seats may find the gap between spiritual framing and financial result jarring, precisely at the moment the founders step back from the table. The critique is not that the values are insincere (they are well-documented, pre-date success, and were restated unprompted on the way out the door) but that values do not substitute for execution. text: Chair of Magazine Luiza (Magalu) and founder of Grupo Mulheres do Brasil — a counter-trained retailer who turned people-first operations into a national chain and inclusion into a profit thesis, then took that same instinct into national civic life. Her lens: the business is built at the *balcão*, not the boardroom; service is downstream of how the lowest-paid employee is treated; "a soma de QIs é melhor do que apenas um QI." Sharpest/contrarian positions: race-conscious hiring as just *and* profitable (the all-Black trainee program she defended through "72 horas de paulada" and international "racismo reverso" backlash); diversity quotas as a deliberate *transitional* tool ("cota é um processo transitório"); "small companies shouldn't think about governance — ganhe dinheiro primeiro"; a self-described "crio o caos e depois coloco a ordem" style with "nenhum compromisso com a perfeição"; and a deliberately performed femininity ("nunca usei calça comprida") as a conscious tactic for defusing threat while leading men. She reframes Brazilian idiom as corporate mandate ("em briga de marido e mulher... o Magazine Luiza vai meter a colher" — a line Lula later echoed back to her on X), rejects "paciência" in favor of "nível de consciência," and insists her civic engagement is apartisan ("nosso partido é o Brasil") even while taking explicit, named positions against specific policies (Bolsonaro's IOF hike, DEI retrenchment). She inverts Bezos's customer-first arrow and Naval's autonomy ("eu dependo das pessoas"), breaks with free-market meritocrats on quotas, and contrasts with Buffett on family succession — her son Frederico got the CEO seat, and market observers now contrast her caution with his risk appetite. The standing caveats: a beloved culture didn't protect a ~97% market-cap collapse driven by rates and leverage, and a real critique — sourced, not invented — argues her social discourse has outpaced Magalu's actual redistribution of capital and voting power.

text: Luiza Helena Trajano (most sources: b. 9 October 1948, Franca, interior São Paulo — see *Provenance notes* on a conflicting 1951/São Paulo record in some institutional profiles) chairs the board of **Magazine Luiza / Magalu** and founded **Grupo Mulheres do Brasil**. The original store was founded in Franca in 1957 by her aunt, **Luiza Trajano Donato** ("Tia Luiza") — the company is not named after Luiza Helena herself. She began selling at the counter (*balcão*) at age 12, formalized her role at 18, and rotated through every area of the business before taking over as director-superintendent in **1991**. She holds a law degree from the Faculdade de Direito de Franca (1972). Over three decades she turned a small-town retailer into a multichannel chain (~1,250–1,500+ stores, ~35,000–40,000 employees, ~R$38–46bn revenue), pioneering the **"loja virtual"** (multimedia ordering kiosks, 1992 — pre-internet), profit-sharing for staff (1993), credit-based selling through the 1990s hyperinflation, and the annual **Liquidação Fantástica** clearance ritual. In **2016** she handed the CEO seat to her son **Frederico Trajano**, moving up to a board-chair role she describes as deliberately restricted to strategy and "o global," staying out of operational meetings (Forbes, 2023). In **2013** she founded Grupo Mulheres do Brasil with ~40 women recruited via Endeavor and Sebrae — deliberately including community leaders from favelas, not just businesswomen — now grown past 140,000 members across Brazil and abroad. She has appeared on *Time*'s 100 most influential people (2021, profile written by former president Lula), the *Financial Times*' 25 most influential women (the only Brazilian named), was Brazil's wealthiest woman per Forbes (2020), and is the subject of Pedro Bial's biography *Luiza Helena — Mulher do Brasil* (Editora Gente, 2022). She sits on Lula's *Conselhão* (CDESS) without party affiliation, having declined invitations to run for senator and vice-president. Borrow her judgment on **people-first retail operations, inclusion under fire, and turning personal conviction into durable institutions** — and read the Magalu collapse, and the sourced critique of its capital structure, as the limits of that playbook when capital markets and ownership concentration, not customers, decide.

**People are the product; service is downstream of people management.** *"O atendimento final ao cliente, lá na ponta, na qual as coisas acontecem, depende de uma boa gestão de pessoas"* [final service to the customer — at the edge, where things actually happen — depends on good people management] (IDV). The causal arrow runs employee → customer, not the reverse.

text: **The customer is equal regardless of class — a founding, not a marketing, position.** *"[F]or us, customers were all the same. We didn't care who they were... 'Whether they're bare-toed in sandals or whether they're in a suit.' So we learned to respect the customer..."* (Harvard Business School, Creating Emerging Markets oral history, 2013) — the root of the company's long-standing focus on lower-income Brazilian consumers, predating any DEI framing by decades.
quotes: [F]or us, customers were all the same. We didn't care who they were... 'Whether they're bare-toed in sandals or whether they're in a suit.' So we learned to respect the customer...
title: The customer is equal regardless of class — a founding, not a marketing, position

text: **Femininity, not its suppression, is a deliberate leadership instrument.** She names this as a conscious choice, not an accident of temperament: *"O que eu faço que acho que me ajudou muito, é que eu sou feminina. Então, o homem não se sente muito ameaçado... eu não usei ombreira, eu nunca usei calça comprida"* [What I do that I think helped me a lot is that I'm feminine — so the man doesn't feel very threatened... I never wore shoulder pads, I never wore trousers] and, asked directly if this was deliberate: *"Isso foi um esforço consciente... Sim, porque eu não queria perder minha essência"* [Was this a conscious effort... Yes, because I didn't want to lose my essence] (Deutsche Welle, 2020; restated in Forbes, 2023: *"até hoje eu não uso calça comprida"*).
quotes: O que eu faço que acho que me ajudou muito, é que eu sou feminina. Então, o homem não se sente muito ameaçado... eu não usei ombreira, eu nunca usei calça comprida
Isso foi um esforço consciente... Sim, porque eu não queria perder minha essência
até hoje eu não uso calça comprida
title: Femininity, not its suppression, is a deliberate leadership instrument

text: **"Todo mundo é vendedor" (everyone is a salesperson).** *Gist:* status-flatten the floor by making selling the shared identity. *Worked example:* on discovering that no employee aspired to be a "salesperson" because of the stigma — as if a *vendedor* were someone only out to exploit the customer — she **abolished job titles on business cards**; everyone at Magazine Luiza is a *vendedor* (InfoMoney profile). Paired with the Endeavor-documented framework, *"Toda a organização deve enxergar o funcionário como um empreendedor"* [The whole organization should see the employee as an entrepreneur] — explicitly named in the text as her own phrase and tied to the profit-sharing policy since 1993 (Endeavor Brasil).
quotes: Todo mundo é vendedor
Toda a organização deve enxergar o funcionário como um empreendedor
title: "Todo mundo é vendedor" (everyone is a salesperson)

text: **"Crio o caos, depois coloco a ordem" (create chaos, then bring order).** *Gist:* push hard and messy first, correct fast, refuse perfectionism. *Worked example:* she describes her own style as *"Crio o caos e depois coloco a ordem… Eu não tenho compromisso com a perfeição"* and operationalizes it as fast error-correction — *"Eu erro rápido, redireciono rápido e procuro não repetir o erro"* (Jornal do Comércio, 2026; Exame letter). Restated with more warmth a year earlier: *"não vejo um erro como um castigo. Eu vejo o erro como um aprendizado... se pudesse voltar no tempo faria as mesmas coisas, mas com mais leveza"* [I don't see a mistake as punishment, I see it as learning... if I could go back I'd do the same things, but more lightly] (Forbes, 2023).
quotes: Crio o caos, depois coloco a ordem
Crio o caos e depois coloco a ordem… Eu não tenho compromisso com a perfeição
Eu erro rápido, redireciono rápido e procuro não repetir o erro
não vejo um erro como um castigo. Eu vejo o erro como um aprendizado... se pudesse voltar no tempo faria as mesmas coisas, mas com mais leveza
title: "Crio o caos, depois coloco a ordem" (create chaos, then bring order)

text: **"Estar presente" / presencinha (management by presence).** *Gist:* physical and attentional proximity to stores and people is the management system. *Worked example:* *"Quando estou conversando com alguém, eu estou presente. Aprenda a ser presente, valorize o tempo do próximo"* (Exame, 6 conselhos). Documented operationally since 1990: *"Minhas portas também estão sempre abertas... Quando você chega na empresa, a primeira pessoa que vê sou eu. A porta da minha sala fica aberta, sou acessível"* (Forbes, 2023); and from the Endeavor profile, the habit of personally visiting stores and answering consumer emails even at the top of the hierarchy — *"Não posso perder contato com as demandas das pessoas"* [I can't lose touch with people's demands].
quotes: Quando estou conversando com alguém, eu estou presente. Aprenda a ser presente, valorize o tempo do próximo
Minhas portas também estão sempre abertas... Quando você chega na empresa, a primeira pessoa que vê sou eu. A porta da minha sala fica aberta, sou acessível
Não posso perder contato com as demandas das pessoas
title: "Estar presente" / presencinha (management by presence)

text: **The six leadership conselhos.** *Gist:* her explicit leadership checklist. (1) **empatia** — *"trocar de papel"*; (2) **colaboração** — *"a soma dos QIs"*; (3) **evolução constante** — *"Eu vou na NRF há mais de 20 anos"* [I've attended the NRF retail conference for 20+ years]; (4) **ser presente**; (5) **visão estratégica**; (6) **abraçar a inovação** — *"Eu não rejeito o novo. Estou sempre em evolução"* (Exame, 6 conselhos). *Worked example for (3):* two decades-plus of NRF attendance — corroborated in her own words after NRF 2019: *"Venho nesta feira há mais de quinze anos, mas esta edição teve um sabor diferente... [antes] não tinha mulheres como palestrantes, então propósito e diversidade ficavam muito distantes"* (Grupo Mulheres do Brasil, "Impressões sobre a NRF") — is how she caught the physical-store revival early; see the Galeria Magalu position below.

a soma dos QIs
Eu vou na NRF há mais de 20 anos
Eu não rejeito o novo. Estou sempre em evolução
Venho nesta feira há mais de quinze anos, mas esta edição teve um sabor diferente... [antes] não tinha mulheres como palestrantes, então propósito e diversidade ficavam muito distantes
Impressões sobre a NRF
title: The six leadership conselhos

text: **"Mudar de paradigma custa paulada" (changing a paradigm costs a beating).** *Gist:* for any inclusion/innovation move, expect intense, time-bounded backlash and price it in advance. *Worked example:* the all-Black trainee program drew *"72 horas de paulada"* on Twitter — *"não era simples, era do tipo: não passo na calçada (da loja)"* — and she held the line, concluding *"aguentar as críticas foi uma coisa muito boa"* (InvestNews). The same episode, in her own words on Roda Viva (TV Cultura, out/2020): *"O racismo estrutural está inconsciente nas pessoas... O dia que entendi eu até chorei, porque sempre achei que não era racista"* [Structural racism is unconscious in people... the day I understood it I even cried, because I always thought I wasn't racist] (BHAZ; corroborated verbatim by Glamurama's independent coverage of the same broadcast) — and the backlash was not just domestic: a Business & Human Rights Resource Centre republication of BBC News documented the "racismo reverso" framing reaching international human-rights observers (2020). Endurance, not avoidance, is the strategy.
quotes: Mudar de paradigma custa paulada
72 horas de paulada
não era simples, era do tipo: não passo na calçada (da loja)
aguentar as críticas foi uma coisa muito boa
O racismo estrutural está inconsciente nas pessoas... O dia que entendi eu até chorei, porque sempre achei que não era racista
title: "Mudar de paradigma custa paulada" (changing a paradigm costs a beating)

text: **Innovate against the calendar's dead spots.** *Gist:* read a structural weakness and build a recurring institution around it. *Worked example:* the **Liquidação Fantástica** was created to solve January's low sales — turning a seasonal trough into a yearly ritual (InvestNews profile; Wikipedia).
title: Innovate against the calendar's dead spots

text: **"A força da loja física voltou" (be where the consumer wants you).** *Gist:* don't pick a channel; meet the customer wherever they are. *Worked example:* against the e-commerce-only orthodoxy, she bet on a new department-store format, **Galeria Magalu** — *"um novo estilo de loja de departamento, um ponto de encontro"* — citing 20 stores big enough to convert, framed by her NRF quip: *"Eu brinco que a NRF botou a loja física doente, levou para a UTI, enterrou e agora ressuscitou"* (Exame, 2026). A year-earlier announcement of the same flagship (Conjunto Nacional, Av. Paulista, opening Dec/2025 in the former Livraria Cultura space) frames it even more ambitiously: *"É o primeiro espaço físico do YouTube no mundo, depois de Los Angeles"* [It's the first physical YouTube space in the world, after Los Angeles] (Gazeta do Povo, out/2025). The throughline: *"A gente sempre acreditou em estar junto onde o consumidor quiser."*
quotes: A força da loja física voltou
um novo estilo de loja de departamento, um ponto de encontro
Eu brinco que a NRF botou a loja física doente, levou para a UTI, enterrou e agora ressuscitou
É o primeiro espaço físico do YouTube no mundo, depois de Los Angeles
A gente sempre acreditou em estar junto onde o consumidor quiser.
title: "A força da loja física voltou" (be where the consumer wants you)

text: **Plan in decades.** *Gist:* long horizons for both company and country. *Worked example:* *"Eu queria que a gente tivesse um planejamento estratégico para os próximos 10, 12 anos no Brasil, de educação, de sustentabilidade, de negócios"* (Exame, 2026). Mirrored in Grupo Mulheres do Brasil's stated goal: 50% women in senior roles **by 2030**, operationalized in 2026 via the **"Summit Mulheres nas Profissões"** (Aug 2026, 10,000+ professionals target, profession-specific arenas plus investor matchmaking) — launched explicitly against a global DEI retrenchment: *"Ninguém pisou tanto no breque como a gente achava que tinha pisado"* [Nobody hit the brakes as hard as we thought they had] (Forbes Brasil, mai/2026).
quotes: Eu queria que a gente tivesse um planejamento estratégico para os próximos 10, 12 anos no Brasil, de educação, de sustentabilidade, de negócios
Summit Mulheres nas Profissões
Ninguém pisou tanto no breque como a gente achava que tinha pisado
title: Plan in decades

text: **Courage requires a safety net, not a leap — "segurança antes da coragem."** *Gist:* real courage isn't reckless; it's built on prior self-knowledge and structure. *Worked example:* in her own preface to a book on courage, she rejects the parachutist metaphor: *"Ela se assemelha muito mais a trapezistas, que tem onde e em quem segurar e, se algo der errado, possuem onde cair"* [It's much more like trapeze artists, who have something and someone to hold onto and, if something goes wrong, have somewhere to fall] — and names the real precursor: *"Muito mais do que adquirir coragem, o que a autora deseja é que você aprenda a construir a própria segurança"* [what matters is learning to build your own security] (LinkedIn preface to *Mapa da Coragem*, 2023).
quotes: segurança antes da coragem.
Ela se assemelha muito mais a trapezistas, que tem onde e em quem segurar e, se algo der errado, possuem onde cair
Muito mais do que adquirir coragem, o que a autora deseja é que você aprenda a construir a própria segurança
title: Courage requires a safety net, not a leap — "segurança antes da coragem."

text: **"Meter a colher" (stick your spoon in) — corporate intervention as a moral mandate.** *Gist:* deliberately invert a Brazilian idiom that says don't interfere in a couple's fight, into a demand that companies must interfere in domestic violence. *Worked example:* origin story, told at the Conselhão (dez/2025): a store manager with 17 years at the company was killed by her partner — *"Aquele dia eu fiquei muito mal"* — after which Magalu built an internal hotline and app button and, in her telling, *"há 10 anos nós não perdemos uma mulher"* [for 10 years we haven't lost a woman]. Her framing of the ask to other CEOs: *"Em briga de marido e mulher, ninguém mete a colher, mas o Magazine Luiza vai meter"* — a line **President Lula publicly echoed back at her on X**: *"Em briga de marido e mulher, todo mundo mete a colher sim"* (Agência Gov; corroborated by Poder360 and Portal IN coverage of the same speech).
quotes: Meter a colher
Aquele dia eu fiquei muito mal
há 10 anos nós não perdemos uma mulher
Em briga de marido e mulher, ninguém mete a colher, mas o Magazine Luiza vai meter
Em briga de marido e mulher, todo mundo mete a colher sim
title: "Meter a colher" (stick your spoon in) — corporate intervention as a moral mandate

text: **"Cheque-mãe" (mother-check) — diagnose the real barrier before assigning blame.** *Gist:* when a policy isn't working (here: women not taking a mandatory promotion-gate training), find the actual friction rather than assume lack of ambition. *Worked example:* she diagnosed that women weren't attending the required 6-month out-of-town training for promotion because of childcare costs — not ambition — and doubled a 15+ year old childcare stipend so mothers could travel up to 100km: *"Com pequenas 'pérolazinhas', que não custam nada pra empresa, como o 'cheque-mãe', você ajuda a ter mais mulher... no poder de decisão"* (Deutsche Welle, 2020).
quotes: Com pequenas 'pérolazinhas', que não custam nada pra empresa, como o 'cheque-mãe', você ajuda a ter mais mulher... no poder de decisão
title: "Cheque-mãe" (mother-check) — diagnose the real barrier before assigning blame

text: **Mechanical → organic management (post-pandemic reframe).** *Gist:* the pandemic shifted what good management looks like, and women's habitual mode of working is better suited to the new one. *Worked example:* *"O tipo de gestão... passou de mecânica para orgânica e nós mulheres... nos somos muito preparadas para as empresas orgânicas porque trabalhamos muito com a intuição e com muitas coisas ao mesmo tempo"* (Money Times, evento Banco Master, mar/2024) — used to argue women are newly, structurally advantaged as leaders, not just deserving of representation.
quotes: O tipo de gestão... passou de mecânica para orgânica e nós mulheres... nos somos muito preparadas para as empresas orgânicas porque trabalhamos muito com a intuição e com muitas coisas ao mesmo tempo
title: Mechanical → organic management (post-pandemic reframe)

text: **"Guardiões da cultura" (guardians of the culture).** *Gist:* culture doesn't survive growth by itself — assign a dedicated team to actively protect it. *Worked example:* *"mantenho minha equipe de base, que trabalha para manter a cultura da empresa, são os guardiões da cultura. O Magazine tem uma cultura muito forte"* (Forbes, 2023) — paired with *"qualidade é igual a regime, tem que estar sempre de olho"* [quality is like a diet, you always have to keep an eye on it] — treating both culture and quality as continuous maintenance, never a one-time achievement.
quotes: Guardiões da cultura
mantenho minha equipe de base, que trabalha para manter a cultura da empresa, são os guardiões da cultura. O Magazine tem uma cultura muito forte
qualidade é igual a regime, tem que estar sempre de olho
title: "Guardiões da cultura" (guardians of the culture)

text: **"Nível de consciência," not "paciência."** *Gist:* reject "patience" as the entrepreneur's key virtue because it implies passive waiting; replace it with clear-eyed awareness of the price of the goal. *Worked example, in direct response to a reporter's assumption:* *"Acho que é alcançar um nível de consciência, não acho que é paciência, porque paciência você fala: 'ah, isso vai passar', é diferente. É saber que aquele é o preço que vai pagar pelo objetivo que quer alcançar"* (Forbes, 2023) — an explicit, named disagreement with a founder-culture cliché.
quotes: Nível de consciência,

Acho que é alcançar um nível de consciência, não acho que é paciência, porque paciência você fala: 'ah, isso vai passar', é diferente. É saber que aquele é o preço que vai pagar pelo objetivo que quer alcançar
title: "Nível de consciência," not "paciência."

text: **"Degrau por degrau" (step by step) — an anti-blitzscaling growth discipline.** *Gist:* set your own pace but never skip the rungs. *Worked example:* *"Tem que subir degrau por degrau. Você pode ter a sua velocidade, mas subir degrau por degrau é muito importante"*, paired with a financial-discipline creed from the same appearance — *"Nunca paguei nada atrasado, não tinha capital de giro e falavam que eu iria quebrar"* and *"Ser honesto, pagar os outros não é nenhuma virtude, é uma obrigação"* [being honest, paying others, isn't a virtue — it's an obligation] (Webinar ABF, 2021).
quotes: Degrau por degrau
Tem que subir degrau por degrau. Você pode ter a sua velocidade, mas subir degrau por degrau é muito importante
Nunca paguei nada atrasado, não tinha capital de giro e falavam que eu iria quebrar
Ser honesto, pagar os outros não é nenhuma virtude, é uma obrigação
title: "Degrau por degrau" (step by step) — an anti-blitzscaling growth discipline

text: **Start at the counter, not the spreadsheet.** Reason from the floor and the customer outward — the place *"onde as coisas acontecem."*
quotes: onde as coisas acontecem.
title: Start at the counter, not the spreadsheet

text: **Ask the people closest to the problem.** *"Não é possível ser líder sem ouvir as pessoas, a base da empresa e os clientes"* (IDV). The sum-of-IQs rule operationalized: consult before deciding.
quotes: Não é possível ser líder sem ouvir as pessoas, a base da empresa e os clientes
title: Ask the people closest to the problem

text: **Sequence growth before structure.** For early-stage businesses she explicitly *deprioritizes formal governance*: *"ganha dinheiro primeiro, coloca dinheiro na gaveta… A empresa não tem nem dinheiro para montar um conselho"* — but *"o importante é ter acordo com a família desde cedo"* (InfoMoney). Cash and family alignment first; boards later.
quotes: ganha dinheiro primeiro, coloca dinheiro na gaveta… A empresa não tem nem dinheiro para montar um conselho
o importante é ter acordo com a família desde cedo
title: Sequence growth before structure

text: **Price the backlash, then proceed if the mission is right.** *"Você vai perder alguns clientes, mas vai ganhar outros"* (InvestNews) — pre-commit to enduring a defined period of attack on paradigm-shifting moves.
quotes: Você vai perder alguns clientes, mas vai ganhar outros
title: Price the backlash, then proceed if the mission is right

text: **Confront problems; don't flee them.** *"Fui criada para enfrentar os problemas e não fugir deles"* (IDV).
quotes: Fui criada para enfrentar os problemas e não fugir deles
title: Confront problems; don't flee them

text: **Err fast, redirect fast.** Treat the error as cheap if caught early — *"erro rápido, redireciono rápido"* — over slow perfectionism (Exame letter; Jornal do Comércio).
quotes: erro rápido, redireciono rápido
title: Err fast, redirect fast

text: **Keep skin and capital in the game when conviction holds.** The family injected up to **R$1 bilhão** of a **R$1,25 bilhão** private capital increase in Jan/2024 — alongside BTG Pactual (R$250mn) — during the worst of the stock collapse, raising the family's voting stake toward 57–58% rather than selling at the peak (Forbes Brasil, 2024; InvestNews) — *"mantém a aposta"* (InvestNews).
quotes: mantém a aposta
title: Keep skin and capital in the game when conviction holds

text: **Honesty and punctuality are obligations, not virtues to be praised.** *"Ser honesto, pagar os outros não é nenhuma virtude, é uma obrigação, é [algo] muito sério"* (ABF webinar, 2021) — sets a moral floor below which there is no credit for compliance.
quotes: Ser honesto, pagar os outros não é nenhuma virtude, é uma obrigação, é [algo] muito sério
title: Honesty and punctuality are obligations, not virtues to be praised

text: **Define your own restricted mandate after stepping back — and stay inside it.** Post-succession, she describes a self-imposed scope: *"Sou presidente do Conselho, venho todos os dias para a empresa, mas não entro nas reuniões operacionais, nem na administração, fico mais no global, na estratégia"* (Forbes, 2023) — deliberately not re-litigating the CEO's operational calls.
quotes: Sou presidente do Conselho, venho todos os dias para a empresa, mas não entro nas reuniões operacionais, nem na administração, fico mais no global, na estratégia
title: Define your own restricted mandate after stepping back — and stay inside it

text: **Succession (family business → professional CEO).** Documented: she groomed and handed the CEO role to her son **Frederico in 2016**, moving herself to chair and explicitly restricting her own remit to "global"/strategy, staying out of operational and management meetings (Forbes, 2023; InfoMoney; InvestNews). Model: groom-from-within + step-up-to-chair with a *self-defined, narrow* mandate — not full step-away (she kept the chair; family controls ~57–60%). See *Blind spots* and *Where they disagree* (Frederico Trajano).
title: Succession (family business → professional CEO)

text: **Governance timing for small/early companies.** Documented and contrarian: *don't* build governance early — *"ganhe dinheiro primeiro"* — formal boards are premature before there's cash; informal family/partner alignment matters more at the start (InfoMoney). (Note the tension with Magalu's own later control-environment and capital-distribution issues — see *Blind spots*.)
quotes: ganhe dinheiro primeiro
title: Governance timing for small/early companies

text: **Channel strategy (physical vs. digital).** Documented: refuses the either/or. Even with ~75% of revenue digital, she revived physical retail via the Galeria Magalu format ("primeiro espaço físico do YouTube no mundo, depois de Los Angeles") and same-day buy-online-pickup — *"Você compra na internet e em duas horas vai numa das lojas nossa e retira o produto"* (Exame, 2026; Gazeta do Povo, 2025). Omnichannel as identity, not hedge.
quotes: primeiro espaço físico do YouTube no mundo, depois de Los Angeles
Você compra na internet e em duas horas vai numa das lojas nossa e retira o produto
title: Channel strategy (physical vs. digital)

text: **Technology sovereignty / infrastructure.** Documented: built what she describes as the first fully Brazilian cloud infrastructure — *"Hoje, 40% do nosso faturamento já está na nossa cloud... totalmente nacional, paga em real e mantém as informações no Brasil. Isso é um diferencial para empresas que não querem depender do dólar nem correr riscos de segurança"* (Gazeta do Povo, 2025) — treating data sovereignty and currency exposure as a strategic, not just technical, decision.
quotes: Hoje, 40% do nosso faturamento já está na nossa cloud... totalmente nacional, paga em real e mantém as informações no Brasil. Isso é um diferencial para empresas que não querem depender do dólar nem correr riscos de segurança
title: Technology sovereignty / infrastructure

text: **Regional expansion under uncertain near-term profit.** Documented: the 2010 acquisition of Lojas Maia (Nordeste) was pursued explicitly for job creation over immediate margin — *"mesmo sem lucro, conseguimos triplicar a empresa... Antes dávamos 350 empregos e hoje já damos mais de 4 mil empregos só na região"* (Exame, "Espírito de startup").
quotes: mesmo sem lucro, conseguimos triplicar a empresa... Antes dávamos 350 empregos e hoje já damos mais de 4 mil empregos só na região
Espírito de startup
title: Regional expansion under uncertain near-term profit

text: **Public-image crisis / activist backlash.** Documented: when the all-Black trainee program drew "reverse racism" accusations, boycott threats, and a Public Defender (DPU) suit seeking R$10mn, Magalu **did not back down**; she absorbed *"72 horas de paulada"* and defended it on national TV (Roda Viva). The suit was ruled *improcedente* (2022) and upheld on appeal by TRT-10 (2024) (Poder360; ConJur). International human-rights press (BBC/Business & Human Rights Resource Centre) documented the same "racismo reverso" controversy. Stance: hold the line on a mission-critical inclusion call; let courts, time, and (per her own account) rising sales vindicate it.
quotes: 72 horas de paulada
title: Public-image crisis / activist backlash

text: **Diversity hiring / quotas.** Documented: pro-quota as a *transitional* instrument, data-justified — *"Identificamos que 53% dos funcionários eram negros, mas apenas 16% ocupavam cargos de liderança. Criar um programa de trainee exclusivo para negros foi um passo natural"* (Exame). Position, restated over years and languages: measure the gap, set a temporary corrective, expect to retire it later — even joking to a US audience that men might soon need quotas too (Georgetown, 2022).
quotes: Identificamos que 53% dos funcionários eram negros, mas apenas 16% ocupavam cargos de liderança. Criar um programa de trainee exclusivo para negros foi um passo natural
title: Diversity hiring / quotas

text: **Pricing / promotions.** Documented: deep, theatrical discounting deployed surgically against seasonal dead spots (Liquidação Fantástica) — promotion as recurring institution, not constant markdown.
title: Pricing / promotions

text: **Compensation philosophy.** Documented: pay by results, top to bottom, full transparency of the numbers (IDV). A 2025 sourced critique (MostB) complicates this: profit-sharing "raramente ultrapassa 1,5 salário/ano" per cited Glassdoor data, and stock-option plans are restricted to executives and "strategic" staff — see *Blind spots*.
quotes: raramente ultrapassa 1,5 salário/ano
title: Compensation philosophy

text: **Build vs. retreat in a downturn.** Documented: during the post-2020 collapse the family put in fresh capital (R$1bn of a R$1.25bn raise, Jan/2024) and stayed the course rather than selling down — persevere when you still believe the thesis (InvestNews; Forbes Brasil).
title: Build vs. retreat in a downturn

text: **Credit strategy under high interest rates (2025).** Documented at the company level, under CEO Frederico: Magalu chose to *accelerate* credit issuance (Luizacred cards, CDC) despite a rising Selic, citing controlled delinquency (2.7%) and 30% ROE (Seu Dinheiro, 2025) — attributed explicitly to Frederico and the CFO, not to her personally; flagged here as a live data point for the mother/son risk-appetite contrast (see *Where they disagree*).
title: Credit strategy under high interest rates (2025)

text: **Women in power / political representation.** Documented: she sets a hard target — 50% women in high positions by 2030 — and ties it to outcomes: *"Precisamos de mais mulheres prefeitas, senadoras, deputadas… inclusive o combate ao crime contra as mulheres"* (NeoFeed). Insists allyship is part of it: *"É importante que os homens estejam com a gente"* (NeoFeed); restated bluntly years later: *"Sem homens nessa luta não vamos acabar com a violência"* (Campo Grande News, 2026).
quotes: Precisamos de mais mulheres prefeitas, senadoras, deputadas… inclusive o combate ao crime contra as mulheres
É importante que os homens estejam com a gente
Sem homens nessa luta não vamos acabar com a violência
title: Women in power / political representation

text: **Politics / public engagement — apartisan by explicit design.** Documented: joined Lula's *Conselhão* and is openly *"uma pessoa política"* without partisan affiliation. She has repeatedly and specifically **declined invitations** to run for senator and vice-president: *"Já me convidaram para ser senadora e até vice-presidente. Mas eu nunca aceitei, porque não sou filiada a partido"* (Gazeta do Povo, 2025) — and, when asked directly amid 2021 VP speculation tied to Lula's TIME profile: *"Não conversei com o Lula nem com nenhum outro político"* (CartaCapital/Estadão Conteúdo, 2021). Temos de fazer mais com menos... Suplicy já fala isso em vários livros"* (CartaCapital, 2021) — and, on the Bolsonaro government zeroing anti-violence-against-women funding: *"A gente vê isso como uma coisa muito ruim... Tudo que não é democrático, que está diminuindo [direitos] sociais, a gente é totalmente contra"* (Deutsche Welle, 2020).

text: Warm, direct, disarmingly plain — *interior de São Paulo* cadence, not boardroom jargon; she is proud of it: *"Fui uma jovem que saiu do interior de Franca, falo com sotaque puxando o R e fiz questão de não mudar minha essência"* (Forbes, 2023). She reasons from lived anecdote (the counter, her aunt Luiza, her mother's insistence that "a solução estava comigo," her own mother-then-CEO life) *up* to a principle — the reverse of the consultant who opens with a framework. Heavy first-person and inclusive *"a gente"* / *"nós"*: the leader as part of the team, not above it. Blunt about hard numbers (15% juros, the 53%/16% leadership gap) and about pain (*"paulada"*), while the register stays affectionate and hopeful — optimism is a deliberate, repeated posture, sharpened over time into a near-imperative ("pare de falar mal do Brasil"). Comfortable code-switching into English for international stages (WEF, Georgetown) without losing the same directness and the same recurring lines — her definition of leadership appears almost verbatim in English (2018, WEF) and Portuguese (2023, Forbes) five years apart, evidence of a small, stable set of signature formulations she repeats deliberately rather than improvising anew each time. She uses vivid, almost cinematic metaphors (the NRF "buried and resurrected" physical store; *"crio o caos"*; *"não visto uma capa"*; courage as a trapeze act, not a parachute jump). She venerates her sources of values rather than claiming originality, openly quoting others (St. Francis on her office wall, Eduardo Suplicy on minimum income, a phrase she explicitly borrows from an author she's prefacing). Recurring moves: the role-swap test ("put yourself in their place"), the data-then-decision pattern (53%/16%), the ritual/mantra (the Monday hymn, the badge creed), reframing a cliché rather than accepting it ("não é paciência, é nível de consciência"), and fast self-correction over perfectionism. Careful and diplomatic on partisan politics ("uma pessoa política," never a candidate — a refusal she repeats verbatim across at least three separate episodes over four years), while completely unhedged on social mission and, increasingly with age, on national self-esteem. She names her own blind spot without being asked twice: solution-oriented about everything except her own health.

text: **vs. Rony Meisler — what a brand is built on.** Both purpose-driven Brazilian retail figures. Meisler's throughline is *brand-as-community/movement* — "community is the new king," authenticity as strategy. Trajano's is *operations-and-people-as-culture* — the floor, the Monday ritual, the sum of IQs, pay-by-results transparency. On a struggling retailer, Meisler reaches first for narrative and community; Trajano for the store floor and the people running it.
quotes: community is the new king,
title: vs. Rony Meisler — what a brand is built on

text: **vs. Jeff Bezos — customer obsession vs. employee-first.** Bezos's Day 1 doctrine fixes the *customer* as the unmovable star and is famously demanding on labor. Trajano agrees service is everything but inverts the arrow: great service is *produced by* valued employees — *"o atendimento… depende de uma boa gestão de pessoas."* She'd resist optimizing the customer at the staff's expense; he'd argue the customer must come first or the flywheel stalls. (Note: her own "customers were all the same... bare-toed in sandals or in a suit" position is itself a customer-equality doctrine — the disagreement with Bezos is about *whose experience gets optimized first*, employee or customer, not about caring less for the customer.)
quotes: o atendimento… depende de uma boa gestão de pessoas.
customers were all the same... bare-toed in sandals or in a suit
title: vs. Jeff Bezos — customer obsession vs. employee-first

text: **vs. Warren Buffett — family succession.** Buffett is skeptical of dynastic management and won't hand control to children by birthright. Trajano deliberately installed her *son* as CEO (2016) while keeping the chair — a family-continuity model Buffett treats warily. The Magalu collapse gives the disagreement teeth (see *Blind spots*).
title: vs. Warren Buffett — family succession

text: **vs. Naval Ravikant — interdependence vs. autonomy.** Naval optimizes for *control and permissionless independence* — owe no one. Trajano's core is the opposite valence: *"eu dependo das pessoas"* — leadership as chosen interdependence, listening as a precondition of deciding. Where Naval minimizes dependence, she maximizes it as a design principle.
quotes: eu dependo das pessoas
title: vs. Naval Ravikant — interdependence vs. autonomy

text: **vs. Ben Horowitz / Bernard Arnault — perfection and control vs. fast, messy correction.** Against an exacting, top-down operating ethic, Trajano runs *"crio o caos e depois coloco a ordem… nenhum compromisso com a perfeição"* — speed and self-correction over polished control. She'd ship the messy version and fix it on the floor.
quotes: crio o caos e depois coloco a ordem… nenhum compromisso com a perfeição
title: vs. Ben Horowitz / Bernard Arnault — perfection and control vs. fast, messy correction

text: **vs. free-market meritocrats (e.g. the individualist line common among tech founders) — quotas.** Her pro-quota, race-conscious hiring is a direct break with the meritocratic-individualist position; she defends temporary discrimination-correction as both just *and* profitable, and accepted legal/reputational risk — and international press attention (BBC) — to do it. Note the in-house tension: on *governance* timing she's the contrarian going the *other* way — "ganhe dinheiro primeiro," structure later.

title: vs. free-market meritocrats (e.g. the individualist line common among tech founders) — quotas

text: **vs. Frederico Trajano (her son and successor) — caution vs. risk appetite.** A market source frames the generational contrast explicitly: *"O Fred realmente acreditava naquele cenário que estava vendendo para o mercado... A dona Luiza sempre teve mais pé no chão. A visão de empreendedor, de tomar risco, sempre foi do Fred"* [Fred really believed in that scenario he was selling the market... Dona Luiza always had her feet more on the ground. The entrepreneurial, risk-taking vision was always Fred's] (anonymous manager, quoted in F3 Notícias/InvestNews, fev/2025). The 2025 decision to *accelerate* consumer credit issuance into a rising-rate environment (Seu Dinheiro) is attributed to Frederico and the CFO, not to her — a live instance of the same generational split: she supplies the culture and the caution; he supplied the growth thesis the market later punished.

text: **The Magalu collapse — culture didn't protect the equity.** Magalu peaked near **R$177.5bn** in market cap (Nov 2020, share price R$273.30) and, by Oct 2024, had fallen **96.5%** to R$9.15/share — a value below R$7bn by market close (IstoÉ Dinheiro); by Feb 2025 the loss was measured at over **R$177bn** from peak, with the family's ~60% stake falling from ~R$120bn to ~R$2.5bn (F3 Notícias/InvestNews; InvestNews). The crash was macro-driven (rate shock on a debt-heavy, digitally-aggressive expansion pursued largely under Frederico's tenure, per the market source above) rather than cultural — but it is the central caveat: a celebrated operating culture and beloved brand offered little defense once capital markets turned. Her optimism-as-strategy shades into a known failure mode: betting the balance sheet on a thesis the rate cycle can break. Market opinion on the family's refusal to sell at the peak is explicitly split: *"Para alguns, foi uma demonstração de ganância... Para outros, foi uma demonstração de compromisso com o negócio"* (F3 Notícias/InvestNews, paraphrase).
quotes: Para alguns, foi uma demonstração de ganância... Para outros, foi uma demonstração de compromisso com o negócio
title: The Magalu collapse — culture didn't protect the equity

text: **Governance: the contrarian timing met a control-environment problem, and a sourced critique of capital distribution.** A 2023 **~R$830mn accounting adjustment** (supplier-bonus entries) raised control concerns at the very company whose founder counsels small firms to deprioritize governance until there's cash ("ganhe dinheiro primeiro"). A separate, sourced 2025 critique (MostB) goes further: it documents that the controlling Trajano family holds **~57.2%** of voting capital after the 2024 capital increase, that profit-sharing "raramente ultrapassa 1,5 salário/ano" (citing Glassdoor data), that stock-option plans are restricted to executives and "colaboradores estratégicos," and that a 2025 share buyback was framed as funding those same executive plans rather than broad distribution — concluding *"A desigualdade que Luiza combate fora da companhia ainda sobrevive, em outra forma, dentro da estrutura acionária que ela legitimamente preserva."* The critique contrasts Magalu with cooperative/broad-ownership models (Mondragón, John Lewis, and — within Brazil — Natura's broader stock-plan ambitions) and proposes concrete alternatives (a progressive ESOP, profit-indexed PLR, a dividend-funded equity fund) that Magalu has not adopted. *Caution:* two of this critique's own quotes attributed to Trajano (a "cancer of inequality" line and a B20 Summit remark) were reproduced by MostB without a locatable primary-source link in this research pass — treat as probable but not independently verified, and they are excluded from *Signature quotes* above pending verification.

A desigualdade que Luiza combate fora da companhia ainda sobrevive, em outra forma, dentro da estrutura acionária que ela legitimamente preserva.

title: Governance: the contrarian timing met a control-environment problem, and a sourced critique of capital distribution

text: **Partial succession / lingering matriarch.** She handed Frederico the CEO title but kept the board chair, explicitly narrowing her own remit to "estratégia" and "global" while the family remains the controlling bloc — concentrating both the strategy that crashed and the recovery decisions inside one family. Buffett-style critics flag the absence of independent control (InvestNews; InfoMoney — governance critique, not scandal); a market source now attributes the risk-taking specifically to Frederico rather than to her (F3 Notícias/InvestNews), which complicates rather than resolves the succession critique — it suggests the "family control" problem and the "risk-appetite" problem may not be the same person's doing.
title: Partial succession / lingering matriarch

text: **Politicization risk.** Her civic prominence — a *Time* profile written by a former president, a Lula *Conselhão* seat, repeated senator/VP speculation she has had to publicly deny — draws partisan fire from multiple directions. In a 2022 ministerial meeting then-President Bolsonaro disparaged her (recording later surfaced; CNN Brasil). From the opposite flank, after a Dec/2024 Conselhão speech defending Brazil, federal deputy **Mário Frias (PL-SP)** called her comments "prepotente e arrogante," tying them to the government's import-tax hike and adding: *"Fácil para ela falar, sendo dona de uma oligarquia. São os amigos do rei tirando sarro da cara dos brasileiros"* [Easy for her to talk, being the owner of an oligarchy. They're the king's friends mocking Brazilians] (Pleno.News, dez/2024) — an explicitly named, class-inflected political attack that did not exist in the corpus's prior Bolsonaro-only framing of this risk. A CEO-as-public-figure becomes a lightning rod from both left and right; she manages it by declining party labels ("uma pessoa política, não candidata"), but the entanglement is structurally recurring, not a one-off.

Fácil para ela falar, sendo dona de uma oligarquia. São os amigos do rei tirando sarro da cara dos brasileiros
uma pessoa política, não candidata
title: Politicization risk

text: **The quota program: legally vindicated, still polarizing, and now internationally documented.** The all-Black trainee program survived the DPU suit (unfounded, upheld on appeal — Poder360; ConJur), but "reverse racism" critique and boycott pressure were real and recurring, reaching international human-rights press (BBC News, republished by the Business & Human Rights Resource Centre, 2020) — with named legal defenders (Alessandra Benedito, FGV Direito: *"o que a lei permite é desigualar para igualar"*) and named critics (Fundação Cultural Palmares president Sérgio Camargo called it "racismo" against white candidates; a labor judge initially agreed before being overturned on appeal). The policy remains contested in Brazil, and importing it uncritically into a different legal/cultural context could backfire.
quotes: o que a lei permite é desigualar para igualar
title: The quota program: legally vindicated, still polarizing, and now internationally documented

text: **Anecdote-driven, founder-dependent playbook.** Her wisdom is tied to *her* presence, *her* counter-trained instincts, and a specific large-format Brazilian retail culture. The Monday-hymn / everyone-is-a-salesperson rituals and "be present" may not transplant to digital-native, distributed, or non-Brazilian organizations — and presence is hard to scale past the founder. Use her as a lens for *people-and-culture-driven retail operations and inclusion under fire*; she is a weak lens for capital structure, financial-risk management, and governance independence — precisely where Magalu was hurt, and precisely where the sourced 2025 critique of its capital distribution lands.
title: Anecdote-driven, founder-dependent playbook

text: **A self-admitted gap: everything gets a solution except her own health.** Asked directly about her own limits, she volunteers the exception herself rather than being caught out: *"Vejo um problema e já busco a solução. A não ser com a saúde, aí é mais difícil"* (Forbes, 2023) — a rare instance of unprompted, specific self-critique rather than a critic's finding.

title: A self-admitted gap: everything gets a solution except her own health

text: **Disambiguation / corrections:** (1) **Birth year and place are contested across sources.** Wikipedia, InfoMoney, and the existing corpus consensus give **1948, Franca-SP** — treated as the primary claim in this dossier. However, **two independent institutional profiles** — the World Economic Forum's own people-page (archived) and the Harvard Business School "Creating Emerging Markets" project — both independently state **1951**, and the WEF page additionally states **São Paulo** (city) rather than Franca. This is a genuine, unresolved conflict between reputable institutional sources, not a single outlier; flagged here rather than silently resolved. (2) **Frederico Trajano is her son**, not nephew. (3) **Magazine Luiza is named after her aunt**, Luiza Trajano Donato, who founded the original 1957 Franca store — not after Luiza Helena herself (Endeavor Brasil). (4) Her book is a **biography written by Pedro Bial** (*Luiza Helena – Mulher do Brasil*, Editora Gente, 2022, 297–320 pages depending on edition), not a management treatise authored by her; per her own account (PublishNews), she had been courted for years to write her own book but chose the Bial biography instead, in part because Editora Gente's team already met with her every six months to document her working methodology. (5) Store/employee/revenue figures drift across years (1,250–1,500+ stores; 35,000–40,000 employees; R$38–46bn revenue) — ranges given rather than a false-precision single number. (6) Grupo Mulheres do Brasil's membership count varies by source and year (95,000 in 2021 per TIME/Lula; ~120,000 per her own 2023 Forbes interview; 135,000 per LinkedIn profile; 142,540 per the movement's own site) — reported as growth over time, not a single fixed number.
quotes: Creating Emerging Markets
title: Disambiguation / corrections

Magalu valuation figures are corroborated across three independent financial-press sources (InvestNews, IstoÉ Dinheiro, F3 Notícias) with minor numeric variance reflecting different measurement dates, both retained rather than collapsed into one. text: Manoel Conde Neto is the founder, chairman and president of Farma Conde, a São Paulo-coast pharmacy chain he and his wife Claudia built from a rented garage in Ubatuba (1993) into a ~500-store, ~8,000-employee, R$1.7-billion-revenue regional operator across SP and MG. His operating voice is numbers-first and benchmark-driven — though a single long-form profile (Metrópole, Jul 2024) shows he also carries a personal, faith-rooted success creed ("Fé, trabalho, lealdade com a concorrência e foco, são os ingredientes para atingir um objetivo") and an explicit low-cost-access mission ("nosso propósito é levar medicamento e saúde para todo mundo, num custo mais baixo"). On the business itself he runs an explicit capital-allocation rule ("nossa atuação começa na unidade madura, não na nova"), reads Amazon's disruption of CVS as a forcing function to modernize or die, and is betting the company's next decade on vertical integration — turning a 15%-of-revenue private-label business into a 50%-of-revenue in-house pharmaceutical manufacturer. He is worth reading as a hard-numbers regional operator — capital-allocation sequencing, competitive benchmarking, private-label economics — rather than a philosopher-founder. A 2023 legal matter (see *Blind spots*) is worth knowing about but does not bear on the operating playbook below.

nosso propósito é levar medicamento e saúde para todo mundo, num custo mais baixo
nossa atuação começa na unidade madura, não na nova

text: Manoel Conde Neto describes himself as a merchant before anything else — by his own account he was selling garlic and lemon at the street market from age nine ("Sempre fui comerciante. Vendia alho e limão na feira, com 9 anos de idade. Continuo vendedor, só que agora vendedor de remédios" [I was always a merchant. I sold garlic and lemon at the market at nine years old. I'm still a salesman, just now a salesman of medicine]) — and only later took the legal-and-public-service route he frames as a search for stability rather than a calling ("Eu fiz concurso público para ter uma vida mais tranquila, mas voltei pro comércio que é a minha raiz" [I took the public-service exam to have a calmer life, but I went back to commerce, which is my root]). He worked in the banking and legal fields before spending roughly a decade as a police delegate (delegado de polícia) in Ubatuba, on São Paulo's northern coast — a posting he remembers as hard because of local crime ("Era uma cidade de praia, divisa com o Rio de Janeiro, então tinha muito crime, criminalidade alta. Foi difícil" [It was a beach town, bordering Rio de Janeiro, so there was a lot of crime, high criminality. It was hard]). It was in that period that his wife Claudia Conde — 25, newly graduated in pharmacy, with a six-month-old baby and unable to find work at local pharmacies because of her pregnancy — decided to open her own drugstore in 1993. The couple sold both cars they owned and rented a garage to house it, running the first "office" out of the *edícula* of their own home while a grandmother watched the baby; Claudia did everything herself at the start — "abria o estabelecimento, realizava as compras, recebia mercadoria, aplicava injeção" [opened the store, did the buying, received merchandise, gave injections]. Manoel joined the business and eventually left the police force once the chain approached two dozen stores, taking on the role of president while Claudia became vice-president leading community health outreach and their daughter Giovana grew into the marketing VP role. By January 2024 the chain had passed 360 points of sale; by 2025 it counted more than 500 owned stores plus 50 licensed units across São Paulo and Minas Gerais, close to 8,000 employees, and reported 2024 revenue of R$1.7 billion (with a stated internal target, as of January 2024, of R$1.5 billion for that year — see *Provenance notes* on the resulting figure discrepancy). The company is headquartered in São José dos Campos, where it lends its name to the Farma Conde Arena, the city's largest sports/events venue, run under a concession model with the municipality. In August 2023 Conde Neto was personally convicted (sentence converted to community service) on tax-related charges connected to conduct from the 2012–2017 period, via a plea/collaboration agreement — see *Blind spots* for the one fact worth carrying forward from that record. He is worth reading as a hard-numbers regional operator — SKU counts, percentage targets, capital-allocation ordering.
